markets.fx.cmp.unavailable: There is no currency comparison to make yet. It needs a published rate for the pair and a money market fund in each currency.
markets.fx.cmp.roundTrip: Going in and straight back out costs about {p}%. That is the head start the dollar side gives away before any yield is counted.
markets.fx.cmp.noteBuying: You hold shillings and would convert to invest. You cross the spread on the way in and again on the way out, so your bar is the highest of the three.
markets.fx.cmp.noteHolding: You already hold dollars and spend shillings. The exit spread applies whichever fund you choose, so it cancels and only the yield gap is left.
markets.fx.cmp.noteHedged: You are paid in dollars and spend dollars. You are not taking a currency position at all.
markets.fx.cmp.hedgedBody: Earning and spending in the same currency means there is no exchange rate move that can help or hurt you here, so there is no breakeven to compute. Compare the two funds on yield, fees and access instead.
markets.fx.cmp.hurdle: What the shilling has to do
markets.fx.cmp.hurdleBody: The shilling has to fall {dep}% from here for the dollar fund to draw level, which is {ann}% a year. Anything less and the shilling fund wins.
markets.fx.cmp.raceSub: the last {n} years, both valued in shillings
markets.fx.cmp.record: Every time this bet could have been placed
markets.fx.cmp.recordBody: The dollar side cleared this bar in {wins} of {total} {years} year windows, or {pct}% of them. Past windows are a record, not a forecast.
markets.fx.cmp.aNote: The spread is an assumption, not a quote. It stands in for what a bank counter charges a retail customer, which is several times wider than the interbank legs the central bank publishes. Your own bank's rate is the one that decides this.
markets.fx.cmp.disclaimer: This prices a bet, it does not recommend one. Nobody knows where the shilling goes next, and every figure here is either a published rate or a labelled assumption.

market.note: Yields are net of withholding and are what each manager last published, not a forecast. Hollow points on the chart are months when fewer than ten managers filed: a median from five funds is a sample, not the market, and it misses in either direction. Share of market is the CMA's quarterly return. SACCOs sit in a separate SASRA market and are not counted here.
market.venue.title: The money that is not in a fund
market.venue.saccoBody: Median declared interest on deposits across {n} societies, {j} of them open to join. Not on the ladder above: a SACCO pays once a year, needs membership, and your deposits are not callable. Ranked on deposits, never on the dividend, which is the bigger percentage and the smaller cheque.
market.venue.nseBody: Market capitalisation across the {n} counters that traded. Off the ladder on purpose: a share price is not a yield.
market.venue.nseBodyYield: Market capitalisation across the {n} counters that traded, paying a median {y}% dividend yield. Off the ladder on purpose: that is the one yield here that can lose you the capital paying it.

company.proj.estimateBody: Illustration only, at today's rate held flat. Rates move, so returns aren't guaranteed. Compounded monthly, net of tax.
fund.class.howBody: Longer lock-in, lower fee, higher yield. The classes differ in what they ask of you, not in what they invest in.
fund.growth.derived: Compounded from the completed periods above. The manager publishes no growth figure of its own, so this is our arithmetic on its published returns, not a number it has quoted.
fund.growth.published: As published by the fund manager.
fund.growth.past: Past performance of this fund. Not a projection, and not a forecast.
fund.growth.cagr: The compound annual rate is how fast the money actually grew. A manager quoting an "average annual return" is usually averaging its calendar years instead, which is a different figure.
fund.periods.avg: The dashed line is the {avg}% average since inception.
fund.periods.closed: Published {basis}. These periods have already closed, not a forecast.
fund.comp.source: As of {period} · the fund's CMA quarterly filing
watch.howBody: Out of 10, from the checks Fructa could judge: your statements, how the rate moves against similar funds, its rank, and what its CMA filing says it holds. Notes for information don't count.
